newsitem.title: USA: Incyte, Tibco to build "push" system for drug makers.
newsitem.headline: Incyte, Tibco to build "push" system for drug makers.

text.p: Tibco Software Inc. and Incyte Pharmaceuticals Inc. said Tuesday they will collaborate on a "push" computing system to direct news on drug developments to scientists and researchers.

The system will integrate Incyte's software and databases with Reuters Holdings Plc subsidiary Tibco's patented "push" software, which automatically routs customised information, news and other data to computer users in real time.

Incyte, which is sequencing human genes for a genomics database, said the push system will enable it to deliver the vast amounts of genetic information it generates "in an efficient and customised manner."
"We believe the combination of genomic information with 'push' computing will become a new standard in bioinformatics," said Dr. Randy Scott, president and chief scientific officer of Incyte.

Incyte's LifeSeq database contains information on research on about 100,000 human genes. Scientists use this information to study the way genes work, for example, by comparing the function of genes in healthy and diseased tissue. Incyte said this form of computer analysis sometimes eliminates weeks of work in a traditional laboratory.
With the push system, a scientist researching the breast cancer gene could arrange to have all related information sent to his computer screen as it becomes available.
The idea behind push technology is to send news, sports scores, or whatever information is desired directly to the computer screen, so users do not have to search for it.
Push technology is now used most often in the financial industry to provide real-time stock prices, company information and other related data.
TIBCO was acquired in 1994 by Reuters.
